thread:
ryan-cs: Customer (AcmeBooks) opened a ticket — they see intermittent 429s and a sudden billing spike after traffic shifts to APAC during an EU node maintenance window. They say auth tokens are long-lived; no recent config changes on their side.

jack-support: Can you paste the top-level log lines? Also which API path and model are they hitting?

ryan-cs: path: /v1/generate, model: gpt-xl-2, bursts ~80rps for background batch jobs. Logs: `2026-02-18T14:02:10Z request_id=abc123 route=europe -> fallback=ap-southeast-1 status=429 x-burst-credits=0`. Billing: charges jump aligns with the 429 window.

megan-eng: quick thought — 429s + billing spike when routed cross-region often mean repeated retries plus no burst credit in target region. Also check if fallback path increments cost (cross-region egress).

sarah-ops: Do we have the customer's routing policy pinned? If they had regional affinity, failover might be routing them to capacity-constrained APAC pool which has exhausted its burst credits.

leo-infra: I pulled infra metrics for ap-southeast-1 around that time: sustained qps spike + KV cache cold-starts after maintenance. Burst credits were indeed near 0. We also show increased retry attempts from the client side (exponential backoff but aggressive).

jack-support: Customer says they saw both 401 and 429 in the window — token refresh failing then many replayed requests. Any headers we can ask them to capture to prove flow?

megan-eng: Ask them to capture response headers. Key ones: `x-redwood-region`, `x-redwood-fallback`, `x-redwood-burst-remaining`, `x-rate-limit-type`, and our `x-request-id`. Example repro curl:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

ryan-cs: I sent that to the customer and asked them to attach full response headers. They replied with one sample: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`, headers: `x-redwood-region: ap-southeast-1`, `x-redwood-fallback: true`, `x-redwood-burst-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-type: regional`, `retry-after: 12`, `x-request-id: abc123`.

megan-eng: That matches infra findings. Two contributing factors: (1) EU pool was drained for maintenance so we redirected requests; (2) APAC pool had zero burst credits and was under cold-cache overhead, so throughput dropped -> 429s. The billing spike is from client retry amplification (they retried on 401/429 without jitter) and cross-region egress.

sarah-ops: Immediate mitigations: (a) temporarily bump APAC soft burst budget for AcmeBooks account, (b) enable regional fallback rate-limiter to give smaller steady throughput instead of hard 429 bursts, (c) advise customer to add jitter to retries and respect `retry-after`.

leo-infra: I'll open an internal ops ticket to top up burst credits and adjust fallback window for the next 24h. Also enabling extra telemetry to mark requests that experienced token refresh before request — to correlate auth->retry.

jack-support: For the customer reply: explain root cause (regional failover + exhausted burst credits + client retry pattern) and our short-term fixes. Offer to roll back billing for the amplified portion if they agree to reasonable retry parameters.

ryan-cs: Customer accepted temporary credit bump and will add jitter. They provided a repro script showing the failure consistently when forcing `X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1` header and then killing EU node. They also included `curl` output with the headers above and a stack of 3 retries in ~30s.

megan-eng: Action items:
- leo-infra: top up APAC burst credits for AcmeBooks (done? assign ticket)
- infra: add metric to flag requests that hit fallback + zero burst in same span
- product/console: add clearer UI note on cross-region egress cost when failover occurs
- support: offer billing adjustment and recommend retry/backoff best-practice snippet

ops-bot: Incident ticket #INC-2026-482 created and linked to account AcmeBooks.

jack-support: I'll send the customer a small support writeup with the repro steps and suggested retry policy: `max_attempts=5, base_delay=200ms, max_delay=5s, jitter=true` and note the temporary credit. Closing this thread after confirmation of customer deploys jitter and we verify metrics in 24h. :thumbsup:
